title: Operational Resilience Coordination: 90d Experiment Log & Communications Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working coordination log + lightweight playbook to run a 90‑day cross‑functional program that raises service dependability through targeted SLO alignment, observability hardening, customer‑impact mapping, and communications choreography.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus services: api-gateway, text-gen-inference, kv-cache, embeddings-pipeline (first 90 days).
- Goal is org‑level coordination (platform, SRE, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, customer-success, observability).
- This doc is an operational artifact: daily notes, experiment outcomes, communications drafts, and open decisions.

Primary goals (90d):
1) Establish consistent SLO definitions and incident-to-SLO feedback loop for the four focus services.
2) Reduce 95th percentile request latency for high‑traffic inference routes by 20% under P95 load profile.
3) Close three highest‑impact observability gaps so oncall can detect degradations within 2 minutes.
4) Validate a communications cadence that reduces customer‑facing incident time-to-first-message to 10 minutes for Priority 1 incidents.

Success metrics (tracked weekly):
- SLO adoption: number of services with documented SLOs + owners (target 4/4).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) measured via alert latency (target < 2 minutes).
- P95 lat improvement on inference routes (target -20% vs baseline).
- Customer-first-message latency for Priority 1 (target < 10 minutes).
- Regression alerts fired and triaged within 24 hours.

Stakeholder map (roles & responsibilities):
- Program lead: Priya Patel (platform eng) — overall cadence, cross-team synth, exec updates.
- SRE lead: Ethan Rodriguez — runbook update, oncall training, alert tuning.
- Observability SME: Maya Singh — dashboards, signal definitions, query owners.
- Serving runtime: Omar Alvarez — kernel/runtime opt experiments; test harness.
- Product (hosted API): Sophie Lim — customer impact, SLAs, comms templates.
- Customer Success liaisons: assigned per customer incident.

Weekly cadence (recommended):
- Mon 09:30 — Tactical sync (30m): quick blockers, experiment status.
- Wed 13:00 — Signal review (60m): dashboard walk, open alert smells, new SLO proposals.
- Fri 10:00 — Sprint wrap (45m): decisions, next week commitments, customer comm rehearse.
- Ad-hoc: War‑room during escalations (mandatory for P1).

90d experiment timeline (high level):
- Week 0–2: Discovery & baseline (collect SLO proposals, latency baselines, observability gaps).
- Week 3–6: Rapid experiments (batching tweaks, KV cache TTL adjustments, kernel selection tests).
- Week 7–10: Rollouts & guardrails (canary + rollback playbook, alerting thresholds).
- Week 11–13: Customer comms drill + postmortem practice, finalize SLO docs.
- Week 14: Synthesis & exec readout (lessons, followup backlog).

SLO proposal template (use this for each service):
- Service: <name>
- Objective: what the business cares about (e.g., “API responds to generate calls”).
- Indicator: measurable metric (e.g., downstream-successful-requests / requests_total; tokenized latency P95).
- Target: SLA number (e.g., availability 99.9% monthly; P95 latency < 350ms for short-form routes).
- Measurement window: rolling 30d, burn rates considered.
- Owner: team + primary oncall.
- Customer impact mapping: which customers/features depend on this indicator.

Example SLOs (draft):
- api-gateway availability: 99.95% monthly (owner: product-hosted-api).
- text-gen-inference P95 latency (<= 450ms for sequences <= 128 tokens) (owner: serving-runtime).
- kv-cache hit ratio SLO: >= 85% for hot keys during peak (owner: platform-engineering).
- embeddings-pipeline ingestion success: >= 99% per-hour (owner: data-platform).

Observability hardening checklist (top 6):
1) Tag critical spans with customer_id + route_id for trace grouping.
2) Add P95 and P99 latency panels to default runbook dashboard.
3) Ensure alerts surface both symptom and likely cause (e.g., latency + CPU spin + GC).
4) Build an incident‑impact query: count affected requests per minute by customer tier.
5) Wire regression alerts for model-serving quantization/gpu-change PRs.
6) Create one‑click drilldown links from alert to runbook and trace sample.

Runbook & war‑room play tips (short):
- First 10 minutes: quantify blast radius (customers, routes, regions), set priority, choose comm owner.
- 10–30 minutes: triage cause space (network, infra, runtime, model). Attach a short hypothesis doc to the incident.
- 30–90 minutes: decide rollback vs mitigation. If rollback, run pre-approved rollback job with owner checklist.
- Post incident: write a 1‑page impact note inside the incident ticket within 48 hours.

Communications choreography (internal & external):
- Internal quick alert (slack): P1 triage channel ping includes short template: impact summary + lead + estimated time.
- External customer message (first touch): short, human, expected update cadence. Template stored in Confluence (linked above).
- Exec update: if P1 > 60m include short impact + mitigation + next steps in daily digest.

Experiment examples and quick notes:
- Batching policy A/B: toggle continuous batching on a canary pool for text-gen-inference and monitor P95 tokens/sec and tail latency.
- KV cache suffix sharding: reduce lock contention by sharding hot-key writes, run perf harness for 48 hours.
- Alert noise quarantine: temporarily mute low-signal alerts while we iterate on signal definitions (record changes).

Open decisions / unresolved questions:
- Exact P95 latency targets for long‑sequence workloads — need product tradeoff approval.
- Burn rate policy: what thresholds should trigger automated throttling vs human ops?
- CS play for top 5 customers in high-impact incidents — need to formalize outreach SLAs.

Immediate next actions (this week):
- [Priya] finalize stakeholder contact list and assign CS liaisons (by 2026-01-18).
- [Ethan] audit current runbooks for focus services and list missing fields (by 2026-01-20).
- [Maya] create baseline dashboards and add to shared dashboard folder (by 2026-01-22).
- [Omar] schedule runtime canary for batching experiment on staging (by 2026-01-21).

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Keep experiment scope small and reversible. Prefer runtime flags over code merges for rapid rollback.
- Track customer impact with a small sample of high‑value customers (top 20 by spend) to see real effect.
- Prepare an incident communications dry‑run in Week 10 with stakeholder observers.

Appendix (useful queries & references):
- Example Prometheus: 100ms bucketated latency query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Trace sampling policy doc: confluence link above.
- Template: post‑incident one‑page and P1 slack template stored in linked Confluence index.

-- End of working doc --
